definitions.explanation: Indicates that something has been the case from the very beginning, or that a quality is fundamental and innate. Used to describe original states, inherent characteristics, or the way things were meant to be.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{元来|がんらい}{真面目|まじめ}な{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He is by nature a serious person.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}は{元来|がんらい}{農地|のうち}だった。
{元来|がんらい}{体|からだ}が{丈夫|じょうぶ}だったので、{大|おお}きな{病気|びょうき}をしたことがない。
examples.english: Since I was inherently healthy, I've never had a serious illness.

notes:
A literary or formal adverb. In everyday speech, {もともと} is more commonly used with the same meaning. {元来|がんらい} appears more frequently in writing and formal contexts.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{元来|がんらい}〜な{性格|せいかく}だ — is by nature a ~ personality
・{元来|がんらい}〜だった — was originally ~
・{元来|がんらい}の{目的|もくてき} — the original purpose
